default.description: Please sign in and generate an API Token to begin using the API.

info.description:
Create, update and track short links, QR codes and OneLinks with the T.LY API.

Rate limits apply per user and are shared across that user's API tokens. Creating short links has its own counter. All other documented API endpoints, including listing links, share one general counter. Monthly link allowances apply to the team and are separate from rate limits.

For temporary throttling, honor Retry-After when present. For monthly allowance errors, stop retrying until the allowance changes. See [API rate limits and retries](https://t.ly/docs#rate-limits-and-errors) for the current limits and response headers.
info.title: T.LY URL Shortener API Documentation

get.description: Returns members of the token's team, sorted by name. Use their `id` values in the `user_ids` filter on link lists and team analytics. The response contains names and email addresses; keep it within your integration.

Returns usage and plan allowances for the token's team in one request. Each resource has an integer `used` count and `limit`, including team-specific allowances. `monthly.links` counts short links created in the app or API during the calendar month; `monthly.analytics` counts tracked analytics events. These reset at `monthly.resets_at` in UTC. Custom domains (including pending domains), OneLinks and team members are current resource counts and do not reset monthly. Team members include the owner and exclude pending invitations. A zero limit means no allowance is configured. These allowances are separate from HTTP request rate limits. Usage totals may be cached for a short period, so recent activity may take time to appear. The top-level link and click totals cover short links only; `current_month_clicks` includes this month's visits to older links.
Returns the name and email of the user associated with the API token.

Returns verified custom domains belonging to the token's team. Use the `domain` URL when creating links or filtering short-link lists and team analytics. Include its scheme and trailing slash. Set `include_non_verified=true` to include pending domains; these are not verified for use yet. Set `include_dns_info=true` as well to include DNS details for pending domains. `include_platform_domains=true` adds selectable T.LY-owned domains; these have `is_platform_domain: true` and no custom domain ID. An empty array means no matching domains.

put.description: Updates a short link. Omitted `expire_at_datetime` and `expire_at_views` are cleared, and omitted `public_stats` becomes false. Send their current values to preserve them. Omitted destination, ending, description, password, tags, pixels and metadata keep their current values.

description.description: A private note to help you find the link later, up to 200 characters.

expire_at_datetime.description: When the link stops working, in UTC. Use YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.

expire_at_views.description: Stop working after this many visits. Integer from 1 to 100000.

meta.description: An expiration URL, Smart URLs or rotation URLs for A/B tests. Smart URLs and rotation URLs can't be used together; sending both returns a 422. See the Smart URL options.

password.description: Visitors must enter this password before they are sent on. Use 5 to 100 characters. Send an empty string to remove it.

pixels.description: IDs of retargeting pixels for the link. These replace its current pixels.

public_stats.description: Let anyone see the link's stats.

short_id.description: A new ending after the domain, like `fall-sale`.

tags.description: IDs of tags for the link. These replace its current tags.

post.description: Creates up to 100,000 short links in the background. Send `return_job: true` to receive a job ID and progress URLs with HTTP 202. Poll the status URL every 3–5 seconds until `completed`, `completed_with_errors`, or `failed`, then retrieve any failed rows. Without `return_job`, the response stays HTTP 200 with `true`. Completion emails are sent after all rows finish.

base64.description: A PNG image as a base64 data URI.

put.description: Replaces a short link's QR styling: colors, dot and corner styles, and a logo in the middle. Omitted colors reset to the defaults below, omitted styles reset to square, and an omitted image removes the logo. Include every option you want to keep.

background_color.description: Background color in hex. Defaults to `#ffffff`.

corner_dots_color.description: Corner color in hex. Defaults to `#000000`.

dots_color.description: Dot color in hex. Defaults to `#000000`.

image.description: A logo to put in the middle, as a base64 data URI. PNG or JPG, up to about 500 KB. Send `null` to remove it.

short_url.description: The short link the QR code belongs to.

post.description: Shortens a long URL. You can also set a custom ending, an expiry, a password, tags and pixels, and add Smart URLs or A/B rotation in the same call.

description.description: A private note to help you find the link later, up to 200 characters.

domain.description: The domain for the short link: `https://t.ly/` or one of your custom domains.

expire_at_datetime.description: When the link stops working, in UTC. Use YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.

expire_at_views.description: Stop working after this many visits. Integer from 1 to 100000.

format.description: `text` returns only the short URL as plain text.

include_qr_code.description: Also return the link's QR code as `qr_code_url` and `qr_code_base64`.

long_url.description: The page the short link sends visitors to.

meta.description: An expiration URL, Smart URLs or rotation URLs for A/B tests. Smart URLs and rotation URLs can't be used together; sending both returns a 422. Rotation URLs are the full set of A/B destinations, so include `long_url` if it should be one of them. A Smart URL can set a single `type`, or several `conditions` that must all match. See the Smart URL options.

password.description: Visitors must enter this password before they are sent on. Use 5 to 100 characters.

pixels.description: IDs of retargeting pixels to add to the link. See [List pixels](#pixel-management-GETapi-v1-link-pixel).

public_stats.description: Let anyone see the link's stats.

short_id.description: The ending after the domain, like `fall-sale`. Leave it out for a random one.

tags.description: IDs of tags to add to the link. See [List tags](#tag-management-GETapi-v1-link-tag).

get.description: Returns individual visits and QR scans, newest first, for links still in the token's team. Use `key` as the row identifier. OneLink rows have a null `destination`; visitor details can be null or unknown. IP addresses are excluded. History is limited by your plan, and `earliest_available` gives its cutoff. An empty `data` array is a valid result. To read older visits, send `next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same filters and fixed dates; stop when `next_cursor` is null. This is a paginated history API, not a live event stream. An invalid cursor returns 422. A query timeout returns 503 with `timed_out: true`; retry with a shorter date range.

All operations use the token's team. See the [webhook setup guide](https://t.ly/help/integrations/webhooks) for payloads, X-Tly-Key verification, retries and delivery limits. Deliveries can be skipped when the team delivery rate limit is reached; this is separate from API request throttling. The legacy `event` response field is the first entry in `events`.

post.description: Creates an event subscription. Store the returned `secret` immediately; it is shown only on creation or rotation. Your receiver must accept JSON POST requests and return 2xx. Requires a Business plan with webhook access. All operations use the token's team. See the [webhook setup guide](https://t.ly/help/integrations/webhooks) for payloads, X-Tly-Key verification, retries and delivery limits. Deliveries can be skipped when the team delivery rate limit is reached; this is separate from API request throttling. The legacy `event` response field is the first entry in `events`.

events.description: Events to subscribe to: short_link.visited, one_link.visited, one_link.link_visited. Send at least one and at most 10.

is_active.description: Enable deliveries. Defaults to true on creation.

tags.description: Only deliver events for links with any of these team tag IDs. Up to 50. An empty array matches all tags.

url.description: Your receiver URL. Must use HTTPS and resolve to a public hostname; redirects and IP-literal URLs are not supported. Up to 2000 characters.

get.description: Returns delivery attempts, newest first, with success, failed or skipped status. Retries can create separate rows with different `attempt` values. Logs are retained for seven days. Use `page` while `current_page < last_page`. The list omits payloads, response bodies and secrets. Requires a Business plan with webhook access. All operations use the token's team. See the [webhook setup guide](https://t.ly/help/integrations/webhooks) for payloads, X-Tly-Key verification, retries and delivery limits. Deliveries can be skipped when the team delivery rate limit is reached; this is separate from API request throttling. The legacy `event` response field is the first entry in `events`.

post.description: Requests a test delivery for the first subscribed event and returns 202 with an empty body without waiting for delivery. Set `sync=true` to attempt delivery before returning a JSON delivery result with HTTP 200. A 200 response does not itself mean delivery succeeded: check `status` and `response_status`. Synchronous network or receiver failures can return an error instead of a delivery result; inspect delivery logs after a failed test. Requires a Business plan with webhook access. All operations use the token's team. See the [webhook setup guide](https://t.ly/help/integrations/webhooks) for payloads, X-Tly-Key verification, retries and delivery limits. Deliveries can be skipped when the team delivery rate limit is reached; this is separate from API request throttling. The legacy `event` response field is the first entry in `events`.

sync.description: Wait for a delivery result before responding. Defaults to false.
